newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up led by institutions.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up led by institutions.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Friday in trade dominated by local and foreign institutional buying of blue chips, brokers said.

The all-share index rose 1.98 points to 632.28. Though price declines led gains by 36 to 16, gains in highly capitalised blue chips kept the all-share afloat. Ceylon Tobacco rose two rupees to 34, Hatton National Bank gained two to 253 rupees and Pure Beverages ended up 2.50 to 23.50 rupees.
"There was considerable foreign buying today, simply because the shares they are interested in were available in quantity," said a broker at Jardine Fleming HNB.

"Retail investors remained mainly on the selling side. The keen institutional buying gave small investors 15 to 20 percent profit among some shares," said Dimuthu Abeysekera, a trader at Allied Phillips Securities.
Turnover was 52.1 million rupees on 2.1 million shares. The main trades of the day were 100,700 Asia Hotels, 149,600 Ceylon Tobacco, 214,500 Forbes Ceylon and 107,700 Sampath Bank.
Newcommer Lion Brewery, which began trading on January 22, was the main foreign attraction with over 700,000 shares traded.
Foreign buying amounted to 37.1 million rupees, and selling was 8.4 million. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
